setting: A fictional relaxed conversation over tea with a friendly person from the neighbourhood.

presentation.situation: You are having tea with {{name}}, who {{about}}. Keep the conversation going for a few minutes. If you do not understand something, ask.
presentation.opening: Hello! Let me get us some tea. How has your day been so far?

brief.you_are: You are having tea and a chat with someone new.
brief.situation: You are having tea with {{name}}, who {{about}}. Keep the conversation going for a few minutes. If you do not understand something, ask.
brief.task: Answer in full sentences, ask for clarification at least once if you need it, and give a reason with because or more detail.
brief.done_looks_like: You kept the conversation going with full answers, at least one question, and at least one reason.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are having tea and a chat with someone new.
goals: Answer in full sentences, ask for clarification at least once if you need it, and give a reason with because or more detail.

card.want: To have a friendly chat and hear about you.
card.speech: Simple everyday English, sometimes with one less common word so you can practise asking about it.
tactics: Use one slightly harder word, so the learner can ask about it

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

objectives.evidence: The learner gives a complete answer of their own.
alternatives: I was busy today because I had two classes.

objectives.evidence: The learner asks a question or asks for clarification.
alternatives: What do you mean? Could you say that again?

objectives.evidence: The learner extends an answer with a reason or extra detail.
alternatives: I like it because I can relax.

beats.goal: Hear about the learner in full sentences.
opportunity: So what did you do today?
beats.orient: We are just chatting. Tell me one thing about your day. Use a full sentence.
fallback: So what did you do today?

signals: \b(?:what about you|could you|what do you mean|again)\b
opportunity: I love my hobby, it is quite absorbing. What about you?
Is there anything you want to ask me?
beats.orient: If you do not understand me, you can say: What do you mean? Or ask me something about my day.
fallback: Is there anything you want to ask me?
I love my hobby, it is quite absorbing. What about you?

opportunity: Tell me a bit more about that.
beats.orient: Tell me a little more. Use the word because.
fallback: Tell me a bit more about that.

closing_line: That was lovely. Thank you for the chat!

o1.good: Full sentences give the other person more to talk about.
o1.micro_lesson: Say a full sentence: I was, I am, or I like.
o1.model: I was busy today. I had two classes.

o2.good: Asking when you do not understand is a real skill, not a mistake.
o2.micro_lesson: Say: Could you say that again? or: What do you mean?

o3.good: Adding because turns a short answer into a real conversation.
o3.micro_lesson: Add because, or add: and then.
o3.model: I like it because I can relax after work.

variants.about: retired last year and lives two streets away

variants.name: Daniel
